spec_compliance: mostly true — architecture, layering, and the safety-critical fixes (F1-F4) are implemented exactly as r2/r3 specified; two required deliverables are missing/stale (see blocking_issues)
positive_feedback: compile_module_all / select_kernel / compile_source_with_meta_kernel layering (lib.rs:145-336) is clean and exactly matches §8's signatures. The WRONG-METADATA GUARD is correctly implemented: compile_source_with_meta_kernel builds one HirModule{kernels:vec![selected.clone()]} (`one`, lib.rs:190) and threads that SAME value through both emit_module_bytes and the metadata block (extract_workgroup_dims, kernel_hir.first(), coopmat/shared-bytes/debug-checks reads) — never a filtered-emit/original-metadata split.

select_kernel (lib.rs:260-278) is textbook fail-closed: None+1 kernel -> Ok, None+2+ -> AmbiguousKernel{available}, Some(name) not found -> UnknownKernel{name,available}, empty slice -> AmbiguousKernel{available:[]} rather than a panic. Both DriverError variants' Display messages list every available kernel name (lib.rs:84-89), satisfying the 'never silently pick' + 'lists names' mandate everywhere they surface (CLI, MCP, optimize, fuzz, rewrite-verify).

F1 boundary-safe substitute_strategy_holes_boundary_safe (lib.rs:528-580) is the sound single left-to-right scan the spec demanded: byte-boundary check ([A-Za-z0-9_] exclusion) is the correctness guarantee, longest-name-first is correctly demoted to a tiebreak-only comment, and the doc comment (lib.rs:502-527) is accurate and well-connected to the spec's incident writeup (the `?WG`/`?WG2` -> `1282` miscompile). Comment-scope non-goal is honestly stated inline, matching §4's rationale. strip_all_strategy_annotation_blocks (lib.rs:684-693) correctly loops on 'did this pass change anything' (not token-existence), which is exactly the termination predicate the spec required to avoid hanging on a residual call-form @strategy(...).

F4 winner cross-validation in optimize.rs (run_optimize, cross_validate_winner_module_wide) runs BEFORE both the .spv write and the sidecar write, matching the r3 orchestrator patch precisely — verified by reading the control flow, not just trusting the doc comment.

Per-tool --kernel wiring is genuinely consistent across the full surface: cli.rs (Compile --kernel/--all with clap conflicts_with, Optimize/Verify/Test --kernel), main.rs dispatch, optimize.rs (F3 union_module_holes + F4), fuzz.rs, rewrite_verify.rs, log_opt.rs (correctly kept fail-closed with an updated, accurate message — the pre-existing `kernel` CLI field there is the log entry's kernel-name field, unrelated to multi-kernel selection, and this distinction is not confused anywhere in the diff), and all 5 MCP tools (load_source, enumerate_variants, compile_variant, bench_variant, grid_search) each threading an Option<String> kernel param through to the correct kernel-aware compile surface.

examples/two_pass_reduce.axc is idiomatic and honestly documented: the shared[i32,?WG]-vs-literal-64 deviation from the spec's illustrative text is called out inline (lines 9-21) with a concrete, verifiable reason (parse_shared_len rejects a HoleRef there, pre-existing and confirmed by QA on a clean main worktree), and the barrier-in-loop structure matches §6.1's OQ1/OQ2-safe form (while loop, workgroup_barrier at loop-body top level outside the `if lid < stride` guard).

The QA-fix commit (eb762b4) is a clean, minimally-scoped, well-tested fix: threads `kernel` into resolve_size_shortcut at both call sites, keeps the ambiguous-without---kernel behavior byte-for-byte unchanged, and ships two focused new CLI tests (AT-2963b) that close exactly the gap QA found — no scope creep.
DuplicateKernelName (edge case, HIR lower.rs:343 + validate.rs:391) is implemented and tested, closing the §13 edge case that the parser/HIR previously didn't reject.

minor_issues.description: compile_module_all re-runs the full lex/parse/HIR front end once to enumerate hir.kernels, then calls compile_source_with_meta_kernel(source, Some(name), ...) per kernel, which re-lexes/re-parses/re-lowers the WHOLE source again for every kernel (N+1 total front-end passes for an N-kernel module). Not a correctness issue (front-end is deterministic and this is the same front end used everywhere else), and F4's cross-validator only runs this on failure paths / winner-validation, so it is not perf-hot in v1's expected use (N is small, 2 for the shipped example). Worth a comment or a follow-up if compile_module_all is ever called on a hot path with larger N.

summary: The core FG.9 implementation is high quality and matches the r2/r3-hardened spec closely: compile_module_all/select_kernel/compile_source_with_meta_kernel layering is clean and the WRONG-METADATA GUARD is correctly threaded; the F1 boundary-safe substitution scan is the sound single-scan design the spec mandated (verified by reading the implementation directly, not just the docstring) and is well-commented as the third naive-text-transform fix in the project's history; F2/F3/F4 are all present and F4's ordering (cross-validate before ANY output write) matches the r3 patch precisely; per-tool --kernel wiring is consistent and complete across CLI, MCP (5 tools), optimize, fuzz, rewrite-verify, and the correctly-deferred log-opt; the two_pass_reduce example is idiomatic with an honestly-documented, QA-confirmed-pre-existing parser-gap deviation; and the QA-fix commit (eb762b4) is a clean, well-tested, narrowly-scoped fix. Two items from this review's original explicit mandate turned up real, verifiable gaps: (1) DESIGN.md §3.1.45 was never added anywhere in the diff at that time; (2) the LOC reconciliation QA signed off on (2284/2200) was stale. Both are now closed by the review-fix commit 8fdef92 — see recheck section below. Recommend APPROVE.

`git diff main...HEAD --numstat` across all three commits (7700123+eb762b4+8fdef92): 3144 insertions / 129 deletions total. Applying QA's own established methodology (exclude the non-code milestone spec doc, 539 lines) AND extending the same non-code-doc exclusion consistently to the newly-added DESIGN.md section (29 insertions / 2 deletions, added in this same review-fix pass) gives net code LOC = (3144 - 539 - 29) - (129 - 2) = 2576 - 127 = 2449, independently reproduced by hand-summing the numstat table. This matches the figure cited in the re-check mandate (2449/2200 cap, ~11.3% over, up from the pre-fix 2384/8.4%-over figure because PCR-1's fix + AT-2968c's two new tests add 66 lib.rs lines). Not independently blocking for the same reason the prior review treated the overage as non-blocking: the added lines are a safety-critical panic fix + its regression tests + documentation, not scope creep. Flagging for the record only: no run JSON has yet been updated to state 2449 in place of QA's stale 2284 figure (M3.21-qa.json:65 still reads 'LOC 2284 vs cap 2200') — cosmetic, does not gate this verdict.

Full workspace test run is clean: every `test result:` line across all crates/doctests reports 0 failed. Targeted run of the new tests (`cargo test --package axc-driver --lib at_2968c`) shows both `at_2968c_multibyte_boundary_no_panic_comment_untouched` and `at_2968c_multibyte_adjacent_hole_substitutes_correctly` passing. Read the PCR-1 fix itself (lib.rs): the raw `&source[after_q..end] == name` slice (which panics on a non-char-boundary `end`) is replaced by `source.get(after_q..end) == Some(name)`, which returns `None` (not a panic) on both out-of-bounds and non-char-boundary `end` — correct by construction, since an ASCII hole name can never equal a slice landing mid-multibyte-char. AT-2968c's two fixtures (truncated-candidate-in-comment must not panic and must stay verbatim; full-length-hole-immediately-before-multibyte-char must still substitute) are the right pair to pin both the panic fix and the no-overcorrection property.
